records.text: 1.7.2. You “control” the pieces currently in your friendly Gig area, field, Legends area, and Eddies area. You’re the “controller” of these pieces, even if you’re not the owner.

records.title: Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.

records.title: When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
records.text:
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. If it then gains +2 power, that Unit has 1 power. The order of these effects being applied does not alter this outcome.

records.title: A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number.
records.text: 2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

records.title: Power

records.text: 3.17.1. A card’s “power” determines its success in stealing and fighting. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL.

records.text: 3.17.2. A Unit or Legend’s power is equal to the power printed on the card plus the power of its equipped Gear and any current effect modifiers.

records.title: A Gear’s power modifies the Unit or Legend it is equipped to.
records.text: 3.17.3. A Gear’s power modifies the Unit or Legend it is equipped to.

records.text: 3.17.3.1. Units and Legends inherit power from Gears equipped to them.

records.title: A Gear’s power is not modified by card effects, unless the effect specifically targets the Gear.
records.text: 3.17.3.3. A Gear’s power is not modified by card effects, unless the effect specifically targets the Gear.

records.text: 3.17.4. “Base power” refers to the printed power on a Legend, Unit, or Gear, separate from any applied or inherited modifiers.

records.text: 4.2.1. Legends on the field are both Units and Legends.

records.text: 4.5. You may play a Legend from the Legends area to the field as a Unit by paying its cost.

records.text: 4.10.1. By default, a Gear can be equipped to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend.

records.text: 4.10.2. You can only equip Gear to a card in the field or Legends area.

records.text: 4.10.3. There’s no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit.

records.text: 4.12. When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.

records.title: When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to t…
records.text:
4.12.1. When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to the Unit or Legend in that area.

> **EXAMPLE:** An equipped Unit has the effect “At the end of your turn, return this Unit to its owner's hand.” When you move the Unit to your hand, you also move its equipped Gear to your hand. Once the cards are in your hand, the Gear is no longer equipped to the Unit. So, if you play the Unit from your hand next turn, the Gear does not move with it.

records.title: If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new a…
records.text: 4.12.2. If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new area. The Gear is no longer equipped in the new area, so it stays there when you remove the Legend from play.

records.title: When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order.
records.text: 4.12.3. When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order. Randomize them amongst any other cards bottom-decked at the same time. See Bottom-deck.

records.text: 5.3.1.1. Face-up cards in a public area are known to all players. You can look at information on all face-up cards at any time.

records.title: Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known.
records.text: 5.3.1.2. Face-down cards in a public area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

records.title: If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.
records.text: 5.3.2. If a game area is hidden, these rules apply.

records.title: Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known.
records.text: 5.3.2.1. Cards in a hidden area aren’t publicly known. You can’t look at them unless directed by an effect.

records.text: 5.3.2.2. If a card enters a hidden area, ignore any information on the card and remove any existing modifiers attached to it.

records.text: 5.3.2.3. If an effect requires you to reveal and move a card from a hidden area, you must reveal the card before moving it to another area.

records.title: When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fai…
records.text: 5.3.2.4. When you search for a card in a hidden area, you do not have to reveal any information about your findings if you fail to find a valid target. See Search.

records.text: 5.3.2.4.1. If an effect requires a player to choose from a hidden area using information that is not public, that player may choose to fail to find a target.

records.title: If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choo…
records.text: 5.3.2.5. If an effect requires you to choose from a hidden area without requiring a qualifying card information, you must choose a legal target. You are not required to reveal it.

records.title: If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not cho…
records.text: 5.3.2.6. If an effect instructs you to look at or search cards in a hidden area and does not say what to do with cards not chosen, return those cards to their original area in their original order and state.

records.title: Attack
records.text:
8.15. ### Attack

As an action during your Main phase, you may attack with a Unit. For the full rules on attacking, see ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL.

records.title: “Attack” is a game action in which you spend a friendly ready Unit to attack a valid target, which results in the fri…
records.text: 9.1. “Attack” is a game action in which you spend a friendly ready Unit to attack a valid target, which results in the friendly Unit fighting or stealing.

records.title: You may attack as a Main Phase action.
records.text: 9.2. You may attack as a Main Phase action. See TURN ORDER > Main Phase.

records.title: To attack, you must declare the attack by completing these steps in order.
records.text: 9.3. To attack, you must declare the attack by completing these steps in order.

records.title: Choose a friendly ready Unit in the field area that can attack.
records.text: 9.3.1. Choose a friendly ready Unit in the field area that can attack.

records.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.
records.text: 9.3.1.1. Lagging Units can’t attack. See Lag.

records.title: Choose a valid attack target for that Unit.
records.text: 9.3.2. Choose a valid attack target for that Unit.

records.title: A spent rival Unit is a valid attack target.
records.text: 9.3.2.1. A spent rival Unit is a valid attack target.

records.title: A rival Gig area containing one or more Gigs is a valid attack target.
records.text: 9.3.2.2. A rival Gig area containing one or more Gigs is a valid attack target. (An empty Gig area is not a valid attack target.)

records.title: Card effects may add to, remove, or restrict a Unit’s valid attack targets.
records.text: 9.3.2.3. Card effects may add to, remove, or restrict a Unit’s valid attack targets.

records.title: An effect that allows a Unit to attack only grants the specific permission described by that effect and does not remo…
records.text: 9.3.2.3.1. An effect that allows a Unit to attack only grants the specific permission described by that effect and does not remove other attack restrictions.

records.title: If there are no valid targets, you cannot attack.
records.text: 9.3.2.4. If there are no valid targets, you cannot attack.

records.title: Spend the friendly Unit.
records.text: 9.3.3. Spend the friendly Unit.

records.title: Communicate the attack and the attack target to your Rival.
records.text: 9.3.4. Communicate the attack and the attack target to your Rival.

records.title: When you declare an attack to your Rival, the game process of “attacking” begins immediately.
records.text: 9.4. When you declare an attack to your Rival, the game process of “attacking” begins immediately.

records.title: While attacking, you are the “attacking player.”
records.text: 9.4.1. While attacking, you are the “attacking player.”

records.title: While you’re attacking, your Rival is the “defending player.”
records.text: 9.4.2. While you’re attacking, your Rival is the “defending player.”

records.title: The Unit you spend to attack is the “attacker” or “attacking Unit.” It attacks the selected target.
records.text: 9.4.3. The Unit you spend to attack is the “attacker” or “attacking Unit.” It attacks the selected target.

records.title: If your attack target is a Unit, it’s called the “defending Unit,” “defender,” or “opposing Unit.”
records.text: 9.4.4. If your attack target is a Unit, it’s called the “defending Unit,” “defender,” or “opposing Unit.”

records.title: If your attack target is the rival Gig area, it’s called the “defending Gig area.”
records.text: 9.4.5. If your attack target is the rival Gig area, it’s called the “defending Gig area.”

records.title: When you declare the attack to your Rival, apply effects that last “while attacking” and variations thereof.
records.text: 9.5. When you declare the attack to your Rival, apply effects that last “while attacking” and variations thereof. All effects triggered by attacking or spending the attacker become pending. See EFFECTS > Pending Resolution}.

records.title: After all pending effects are resolved, if the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the att…
records.text: 9.6. After all pending effects are resolved, if the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > Ending an Attack. Otherwise, the attack continues; proceed to the React Step.

records.title: During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react.
records.text: 9.7. During the “React Step” of an attack, the defending player has an opportunity to react. They may take as many reactions as they want, in any order they choose.

records.title: You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.
records.text: 9.7.1. You may only take reactions during the React Step of an attack, and only if you are the defending player.

records.title: You may Call a Legend as a reaction.
records.text: 9.8. You may Call a Legend as a reaction. See Call a Legend.

records.title: You may activate the [BLOCKER] effect on a ready Unit as a reaction.
records.text: 9.9. You may activate the [BLOCKER] effect on a ready Unit as a reaction.

records.title: When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target.
records.text: 9.9.1. When a Unit uses [BLOCKER], it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target.

records.title: You may activate any effects with the [QUICK] keyword as a reaction.
records.text: 9.10. You may activate any effects with the [QUICK] keyword as a reaction. See TERMS > Effect Keywords > QUICK.

records.title: If an effect on a Program in your hand has the [QUICK] keyword, you may play that Program as a reaction.
records.text: 9.10.1. If an effect on a Program in your hand has the [QUICK] keyword, you may play that Program as a reaction.

records.title: If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending.
records.text: 9.11. If a reaction triggers one or more effects, those effects become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before the defending player may take another reaction. See EFFECTS > Triggered Effects.

records.title: At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, th…
records.text: 9.12. At any point during the React Step, while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, the defending player may choose to end the React Step.

records.title: If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends.
records.text: 9.13. If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > Ending an Attack.

records.title: When the React Step ends, the attack continues.
records.text: 9.14. When the React Step ends, the attack continues. If the attack target is a Unit, proceed to the Fight Step. If the attack target is a Gig area, proceed to the Steal Step.

records.title: The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit.
records.text: 9.15. The Fight Step only happens if the attack target is a Unit. If the attack target is a Gig Area, the Steal Step happens instead.

records.title: During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.
records.text: 9.16. During the “Fight Step” of an attack, the attacking Unit and the defending Unit fight.

records.title: At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.
records.text: 9.16.1. At the start of the Fight Step, apply effects that last “while fighting” and variations thereof.

records.title: A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially…
records.text: 9.17. A “fight” is a game process in which two opposing Units compare power to determine at least one loser and potentially one winner.

records.title: A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.
records.text: 9.17.1. A Unit wins a fight when it has a higher power than the opposing Unit.

records.title: When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.
records.text: 9.17.1.1. When a Unit wins a fight, the opposing Unit always loses, regardless of power.

records.title: A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.
records.text: 9.17.2. A Unit loses a fight when it has equal or lower power than the opposing Unit.

records.title: If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.
records.text: 9.17.3. If both Units in a fight have the same power, neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight.

records.title: If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power com…
records.text: 9.17.4. If a card effect says that a Unit wins or loses a fight, it supersedes any win or loss status determined by power comparison.

records.title: When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e.
records.text: 9.18. When you determine the loser(s), any effects triggered by the fight (i.e. “when this Unit fights,” “when this Unit loses a fight,” etc.) become pending. Both players must resolve all pending effects before they may defeat the loser(s).

records.title: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight, resolve the fight’s result.
records.text: 9.19. After resolving all effects triggered by the fight, resolve the fight’s result.

records.title: When a Unit loses a fight, the opposing Unit defeats it as a result.
records.text: 9.19.1. When a Unit loses a fight, the opposing Unit defeats it as a result.

records.title: When a Unit is defeated, its owner moves it to their trash.
records.text: 9.19.1.1. When a Unit is defeated, its owner moves it to their trash.

records.title: A Unit with 0 power cannot defeat a Unit as the result of a fight.
records.text: 9.19.2. A Unit with 0 power cannot defeat a Unit as the result of a fight.

records.title: If an effect prevents a Unit from being defeated in a fight, it is still a loser that has lost the fight, it only ign…
records.text: 9.19.3. If an effect prevents a Unit from being defeated in a fight, it is still a loser that has lost the fight, it only ignores the resulting defeat.

records.title: After resolving all effects triggered by the fight’s result, the Fight Step and the attack ends.
records.text: 9.20. After resolving all effects triggered by the fight’s result, the Fight Step and the attack ends. See ATTACK, FIGHT, AND STEAL > Ending an Attack.

records.title: The Steal Step only happens if the attack target is a Gig area.
records.text: 9.21. The Steal Step only happens if the attack target is a Gig area. If the attack target is a Unit, the Fight Step happens instead.

records.title: If the attacked Gig area has no Gigs in it when the Steal Step begins, no Gigs can be or are stolen.
records.text: 9.22. If the attacked Gig area has no Gigs in it when the Steal Step begins, no Gigs can be or are stolen.

records.title: During the “Steal Step” of an attack, the attacker attempts to steal one or more Gig dice from the defending Gig area.
records.text: 9.23. During the “Steal Step” of an attack, the attacker attempts to steal one or more Gig dice from the defending Gig area.

records.title: At the start of the Steal Step, before choosing which Gigs are stolen, apply effects that last “while stealing” and v…
records.text: 9.23.1. At the start of the Steal Step, before choosing which Gigs are stolen, apply effects that last “while stealing” and variations thereof. Apply any other effects that modify, prevent, or restrict the attacker’s power or ability to steal.

records.title: The number of Gigs an attacker steals is based on its power.
records.text: 9.23.2. The number of Gigs an attacker steals is based on its power.

records.title: If the attacking Unit has 0 power, it steals 0 Gigs.
records.text: 9.23.2.1. If the attacking Unit has 0 power, it steals 0 Gigs.

records.title: If the attacking Unit has 1 or more power, it steals X Gigs (rounded down) according to this formula, where P = the a…
records.text:
9.23.2.2. If the attacking Unit has 1 or more power, it steals X Gigs (rounded down) according to this formula, where P = the attacking Unit’s power.

`X = (P / 10) + 1)`

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit with 1 to 9 power steals 1 Gig. A Unit with 10 to 19 power steals 2 Gigs. Continue this pattern for higher power values.

records.title: The attacking player chooses which Gigs the attacker will steal from the attacked Gig area.
records.text: 9.23.3. The attacking player chooses which Gigs the attacker will steal from the attacked Gig area.

records.title: An attacking player may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value.
records.text: 9.23.3.1. An attacking player may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value.

records.title: If the attacker will steal multiple Gigs, the attacking player chooses the Gigs one at a time.
records.text: 9.23.3.2. If the attacker will steal multiple Gigs, the attacking player chooses the Gigs one at a time.

records.title: If the attacker steals more Gigs than are in the attacked Gig area, choose as many Gigs as possible to steal.
records.text: 9.23.3.3. If the attacker steals more Gigs than are in the attacked Gig area, choose as many Gigs as possible to steal.

records.title: After all Gigs are chosen, apply any effects that prevent or restrict one or more of those Gigs from being stolen.
records.text: 9.23.4. After all Gigs are chosen, apply any effects that prevent or restrict one or more of those Gigs from being stolen.

records.title: After all Gigs are chosen and prevention effects are applied, the attacker steals the Gig(s).
records.text: 9.23.5. After all Gigs are chosen and prevention effects are applied, the attacker steals the Gig(s).

records.title: To steal the Gig(s), move all chosen Gigs from the defending Gig area to the attacking Gig area at the same time.
records.text: 9.23.5.1. To steal the Gig(s), move all chosen Gigs from the defending Gig area to the attacking Gig area at the same time.

records.title: Multiple Gigs are stolen at the same time, each stolen Gig is considered a separate stolen Gig.
records.text: 9.23.5.2. Multiple Gigs are stolen at the same time, each stolen Gig is considered a separate stolen Gig.

records.title: Effects that trigger when a Gig is stolen become pending after a stolen Gig is moved.
records.text: 9.23.6. Effects that trigger when a Gig is stolen become pending after a stolen Gig is moved.

records.title: Resolve all pending effects.
records.text: 9.24. Resolve all pending effects. See EFFECTS > Pending Resolution.

records.title: After all pending effects from the Steal Step are resolved, the attack ends.
records.text: 9.25. After all pending effects from the Steal Step are resolved, the attack ends. See Ending an Attack.

records.title: An attack ends if any of the following are true:
records.text: 9.26. An attack ends if any of the following are true:

records.text: 9.26.2. The attack target is no longer in the area it was attacked in.

records.title: The attack target is no longer a legal attack target for the attacking Unit.
records.text: 9.26.3. The attack target is no longer a legal attack target for the attacking Unit.

records.text: 9.26.4. An effect has ended the attack.

records.text: 9.27. An attack can end before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step.

records.title: If an attack ends before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step, no fight happens and no Gigs are stolen.
records.text: 9.27.1. If an attack ends before reaching the React Step, Fight Step or Steal Step, no fight happens and no Gigs are stolen.

records.text: 9.27.2. If an attack ends while an effect or pending effect is resolving, finish resolving that effect or pending effect.

records.title: When an attack ends, resolve any pending effects that are already pending for the current timing window.
records.text: 9.28. When an attack ends, resolve any pending effects that are already pending for the current timing window.

records.title: After an attack ends and all effects and pending effects for the current timing window have resolved, remove effects…
records.text: 9.29. After an attack ends and all effects and pending effects for the current timing window have resolved, remove effects that last “while attacking,” “while stealing,” “while fighting” and variations thereof. The turn player’s Main Phase continues.

records.title: An effect may include conditions.
records.text: 10.3. An effect may include conditions. A “condition” is a requirement that must be true for an effect to apply, become pending, and resolve. (Conditions are often “if” or “when” clauses.)

records.title: If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.
records.text: 10.3.1. If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.

records.title: A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost.
records.text: 10.3.2. A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost. See Cost.

records.title: A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.
records.text: 10.3.3. A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.

records.title: There are four types of effects: triggered effects, activated effects, permanent effects, and replacement effects.
records.text: 10.4. There are four types of effects: triggered effects, activated effects, permanent effects, and replacement effects.

records.title: A “triggered effect” becomes pending when its trigger condition is met.
records.text: 10.4.1. A “triggered effect” becomes pending when its trigger condition is met.

records.title: You may use an “activated effect” at your discretion during your Main Phase.
records.text: 10.4.2. You may use an “activated effect” at your discretion during your Main Phase.

records.title: A “persistent effect” continuously applies while its conditions (if any) are met.
records.text: 10.4.3. A “persistent effect” continuously applies while its conditions (if any) are met.

records.title: A “replacement effect” replaces one game action or process with another.
records.text: 10.4.4. A “replacement effect” replaces one game action or process with another.

records.title: If both players control pending effects at the same time, the turn player resolves all their pending effects before t…
records.text: 10.13. If both players control pending effects at the same time, the turn player resolves all their pending effects before their Rival resolves all of theirs.

records.title: If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too.
records.text: 10.14. If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too. Finish resolving the current pending effect before resolving any new pending effects.

records.title: If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending eff…
records.text: 10.14.1. If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending effects finishes resolving all of their pending effects (including the new ones) before their Rival resolves their new ones.

records.title: Once an effect is pending, later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving (unless the effect…
records.text: 10.15. Once an effect is pending, later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving (unless the effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution).

records.title: If a pending effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution, that condition must still be true when…
records.text: 10.15.1. If a pending effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution, that condition must still be true when the effect resolves.

records.title: A triggered effect has a trigger condition.
records.text: 10.16. A triggered effect has a trigger condition.

records.title: A triggered effect becomes pending when (and only if) its trigger condition is met.
records.text: 10.16.1. A triggered effect becomes pending when (and only if) its trigger condition is met.

records.title: If multiple triggered effects trigger at the same time, they all become pending.
records.text: 10.16.2. If multiple triggered effects trigger at the same time, they all become pending.

records.title: If the same trigger condition is met multiple times, the triggered effect becomes pending once for each time that con…
records.text:
10.16.3. If the same trigger condition is met multiple times, the triggered effect becomes pending once for each time that condition is met.

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit’s effect text reads "When this Unit steals a Gig, increase it by up to 5.” In this example, the trigger is “When this Unit steals a Gig.” If the Unit steals 2 Gigs at the same time, then the effect “increase it by up to 5” becomes pending twice.

records.title: Lag
Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field.
records.text: 11.3.1. Lag is a condition applied to Units when they enter the field. Units with Lag are also called “lagging.”

records.title: Lagging Units can’t attack.
records.text: 11.3.1.1. Lagging Units can’t attack.

records.title: Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.
records.text: 11.3.1.2. Lagging Units can’t activate [Spend Icon] effects.

records.title: At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.
records.text: 11.3.2. At the end of each turn, all Units lose the “Lag” condition.

records.title: Draw
“Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.
records.text: 11.5.1. “Draw” is a game action in which you move the top card of your deck to your hand.

records.title: When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times.
records.text: 11.5.2. When an effect says “Draw X” (where X is a number), take the draw action X number of times. Literally, it means “move the top card of your deck to your hand, X individual times.”

records.title: When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually.
records.text: 11.5.2.1. When you “Draw X,” draw each card individually. Do not take multiple cards from the top of your deck at once.

records.title: When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.
records.text: 11.5.2.2. When you “Draw up to X,” choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards.

records.title: If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck.
records.text: 11.5.2.3. If you attempt to draw more cards than remain in your deck, it counts as drawing from an empty deck. See GAME OVERVIEW > Lose Conditions.

records.title: [PLAY]
The [PLAY] trigger is shorthand for “When you play this card, [...]”
records.text: 11.20.1. The [PLAY] trigger is shorthand for “When you play this card, [...]”

records.title: The effect attached to the [PLAY] trigger enters pending when you meet all the requirements when playing that card type.
records.text: 11.20.2. The effect attached to the [PLAY] trigger enters pending when you meet all the requirements when playing that card type. See CARD TYPES.

records.title: Triggered effects may use timing labels such as [ATTACK], [CALL], [PLAY], or [DEFEATED], or timing text such as “when…
records.text: 10.17. Triggered effects may use timing labels such as [ATTACK], [CALL], [PLAY], or [DEFEATED], or timing text such as “when,” “at the start of,” “at the end of,” and variations thereof. See TERMS > Trigger Keywords.

records.title: Trigger keywords are a shorthand for specific conditions.
records.text:
11.17. Trigger keywords are a shorthand for specific conditions. When those conditions are met, the effect associated with it automatically enters pending.

> **EXAMPLE:** A friendly Unit has the effect “[ATTACK] Draw 1.” [ATTACK] is a timing trigger. Whenever this Unit attacks, you draw a card.

records.title: Any effects triggered by spending this Unit enter pending at the same time as any [ATTACK] effect(s).
records.text: 11.21.2.1. Any effects triggered by spending this Unit enter pending at the same time as any [ATTACK] effect(s). See EFFECTS.

records.title: [GO SOLO]
The [GO SOLO] keyword is shorthand for “Pay this Legend's cost to play it as a ready Unit.
records.text: 11.25.1. The [GO SOLO] keyword is shorthand for “Pay this Legend's cost to play it as a ready Unit. It can attack this turn. If it leaves the field, remove it from the game.”

implementationDecisions.decision: Choose attacker -> choose/lock target -> spend attacker -> declare attack -> discover and resolve ATTACK effects -> state-based checks -> stop at Rival React. Pre-target selection is an incomplete declaration, not an already attacking Unit.
Targets are spent rival field Units or a rival Gig area containing at least one Gig. Area target carries PlayerId, never a chosen die. No target means no attack; one target is forced automatically.

Use effective Unit characteristic, friendly field control, ready and no Lag. Legends in field are also Units by rule, but their field/Go Solo execution remains unadmitted. No once-per-turn attack counter is invented.
Swordwise's ATTACK trigger occurs once on declaration. Its embedded power condition is checked during resolution through current derived source power; reuse CONDITIONAL_DRAW and DRAW.

After supported pending work, end an invalid attack without retargeting or a fight/steal. No supported trigger moves a participant; trusted post-effect tests exercise the narrow invalidation boundary. Malformed external stable states are rejected, not repaired.
A valid attack stops at RIVAL_REACT with defender acting, empty supported legal actions and explicit UNSUPPORTED_RIVAL_REACT marker/error. Do not auto-pass or advance to fight/steal.
